title: The Galaxy-Brained Burp Quest
description: A talking toilet, seventeen galaxies, a four-thousand-year-old cheese wizard, and one very brave kid with a backpack. Zero vegetables. One hundred percent bonkers.
artStyle: vibrant cartoon illustration, bold outlines, bright colours, whimsical children's book style

nodes.title: The Totally Normal Morning
nodes.prose:
Your name is {PLAYER_NAME}. Yes, that is your actual name, and yes, it is the greatest name in the history of the universe. You are eleven years old, you have a pet hamster named Professor Biscuit, and this morning something very strange happened in your bathroom.

You were brushing your teeth — the good kind of brushing where you mostly just chew on the toothbrush — when the toilet made a noise. Not a normal toilet noise. A TALKING noise.

GLURP BLORP FWEEEE!

"HELLO," said the toilet, in a voice like a frog gargling marbles. "I AM ZORBAX, SCOUT COMMANDER OF THE DIMENSION OF TOILETONIA. WE HAVE BEEN WATCHING YOU, {PLAYER_NAME}. THE FATE OF SEVENTEEN GALAXIES RESTS ON YOUR SHOULDERS."

The toilet stared back — it had grown an eye, which was new. "Also," added Zorbax, "you left your socks on the floor again. That's unrelated but still disappointing."

A glowing golden portal appeared in the toilet bowl and a tiny glowing map floated out. The map showed two paths: one going UP through clouds and stars, one going DOWN through dark tunnels and cheese. The cheese smelled amazing, by the way.
nodes.imagePrompt: A surprised eleven-year-old kid in pyjamas holding a toothbrush, staring at a glowing toilet with one large eye in the bowl, a swirling golden portal visible inside, bathroom setting, vibrant cartoon illustration style, bright colours, whimsical children's book art

choices.text: Dive through the portal HEAD FIRST and shout "I'M IN!"
choices.consequence: No hesitation. Maximum adventure.

choices.text: Ask the toilet some very important questions first
choices.consequence: A prepared adventurer is a living adventurer.

nodes.title: Toilet Portal: Activated!
nodes.prose:
"I'M IN!" you shout, mostly because it seemed like the thing to say, and also because nobody in the history of adventuring has ever regretted yelling something before jumping into a toilet portal. (This is statistically untrue but we're going with it.)

You dive headfirst. The portal makes a sound like a didgeridoo falling down a staircase.

BWOOOOMP — SPLORCH — WEEEE!

You shoot through swirling purple tunnels at roughly the speed of a sneeze. Your hair flies backwards. Your cheeks inflate like a pufferfish. Your left sock somehow disappears — it will never be seen again, and that's okay.

You burst out into bright golden light and land face-first in something incredibly soft. You lift your head. You are on a cloud. An actual bouncy, fluffy, slightly springy cloud, floating above an enormous kingdom built entirely out of other clouds.

Standing in front of you is a round, blubbery creature about the size of a large dog. It has four stubby arms, no nose, and is wearing a tiny Viking helmet. "GREETINGS, EARTH CHILD! I am FLUMF, Chief Wobble-Guard of Fluffaris! The Cloud King has summoned you! The Sky Cheese Moon is falling and only a human with a belly button can stop it!"

Nobody knows why it has to be a belly button. Tradition is tradition.
nodes.imagePrompt: A kid bursting out of a swirling purple portal, landing face-first on a bouncy white cloud, a round blubbery alien creature with four stubby arms wearing a tiny Viking helmet standing nearby, bright golden sky, floating cloud kingdom in background, vibrant cartoon illustration style

choices.text: Follow Flumf to the Cloud King's palace immediately
choices.consequence: Time is short. The cheese won't wait.

choices.text: Ask Flumf what the Sky Cheese Moon actually is first
choices.consequence: Knowledge is power. Also it sounds hilarious.

nodes.title: Very Important Questions
nodes.prose:
You put your toothbrush down. Calmly. Like a person who talks to toilets all the time. "Okay," you say. "Before I do ANYTHING, I have some questions."

Zorbax blinks his one eye. "Fine. We have seventeen galaxies to save but yes, questions, sure, that's fine."

You pull out a notepad from your pyjama pocket — every good adventurer keeps one — and read from your list.

Question 1: Will there be snacks? "...Yes," Zorbax sighs. "There will be snacks."

Question 2: Will I have to eat vegetables? "The dimension you're going to does not HAVE vegetables." This is the best news you've ever heard.

Question 3: Can I bring Professor Biscuit? Zorbax looks alarmed. "The hamster? We have a prophecy about that hamster and we're not ready to deal with it yet. Leave the hamster."

Question 4: Is the toilet going to be weird about this afterwards? "I am a toilet," says Zorbax with great dignity. "I am ALWAYS weird about everything. Now. Are you coming or not?"

GLLRP — BLOOOOB — SHWOOP! The portal expands and you feel yourself being pulled toward it. You grab the edge of the toilet bowl. You can let go gracefully... or grab your backpack first.
nodes.imagePrompt: A kid in pyjamas calmly reading from a notepad at a glowing toilet with one large eye, looking very prepared and businesslike, bathroom setting, vibrant cartoon illustration style, bright colours, whimsical children's book art

choices.text: Let go and fall through gracefully, arms wide like a superhero
choices.consequence: Stylish. Very stylish.

choices.text: Grab your backpack first — a prepared adventurer is a LIVING adventurer
choices.consequence: The string. The sandwich. All of it matters.

nodes.title: The Cloud Palace
nodes.prose:
You follow Flumf across three bouncy cloud bridges, past a cloud market selling things like "Bottled Thunder (Lightly Used)" and "Extra Fluffy Cumulus Chips," and through a pair of enormous doors made from solidified rainbow.

Inside the palace, everything is white and gold and slightly damp in a nice way. At the end of a very long throne room sits the Cloud King. He is enormous — bigger than a school bus, shaped like a raindrop, wearing a crown made of lightning bolts. He has twelve chins. He looks extremely worried.

"YOU!" booms the Cloud King. "The Sky Cheese Moon is falling! In three hours it will land on Fluffaris and we'll all be buried in seventeen thousand tonnes of cosmic cheese! Only a human with a belly button, spun at the correct frequency, can activate the Repulsion Beacon!"

You look at your belly button. Your belly button looks back. This feels deeply unfair.

"How do I spin it at the correct frequency?" you ask. Flumf raises all four arms proudly. "You must do... THE BELLY BUTTON TORNADO DANCE!" He produces a tiny instruction booklet from somewhere in his armpit. The dance has fourteen steps. Step nine is described only as "the unspeakable wiggle."
nodes.imagePrompt: A grand palace made entirely of clouds, white and gold interior, an enormous raindrop-shaped king with twelve chins and a lightning bolt crown on a throne, a child and a four-armed alien creature standing before him, vibrant cartoon illustration style, whimsical children's book art

choices.text: Attempt the Belly Button Tornado Dance immediately — how hard can it be?
choices.consequence: Step nine awaits. You'll know it when you feel it.

choices.text: Ask if there's a simpler, less embarrassing way to save the world
choices.consequence: Dignity is overrated when seventeen galaxies are at stake.

nodes.title: The Sky Cheese Moon: An Explanation
nodes.prose:
"Wait," you say. "What IS the Sky Cheese Moon?" Flumf stares at you. "You don't know about the Sky Cheese Moon?"

"I'm from Earth. Our moon is made of rock. Or so they tell us."

Flumf sits down heavily on the cloud, which bounces him slightly. "Roughly four thousand years ago, the greatest wizard in this dimension — name of Parmelius the Aromatic — tried to build a moon out of magical cheese because he believed a cheese moon would produce better cloud shadows. He was brilliant but also very, VERY weird."

"The cheese has been drifting closer ever since. Until last Thursday when it suddenly sped up."

"Why did it speed up?" Flumf looks embarrassed. "...We may have accidentally shot a catapult full of cloud crumpets at it. As a test. To see if cheese bounces. It bounced. Directly toward us."

BOING! (But in SPACE.)

This is the most ridiculous thing you have ever heard. You also decide it is completely your problem now. You could go find old wizard Parmelius — maybe he can fix his own cheese moon. Or you could search the Cloud Palace for the Repulsion Beacon password, which the Cloud King apparently wrote down somewhere and then lost.
nodes.imagePrompt: A massive golden cheese moon looming in the sky above a cloud kingdom, a four-armed round alien creature explaining the situation to a kid, dramatic cosmic background with stars, vibrant cartoon illustration style, whimsical children's book art

choices.text: Go find old wizard Parmelius and convince him to fix his cheese moon
choices.consequence: Four thousand years old. Smells like a cheese shop.

choices.text: Search the Cloud Palace for the lost Beacon password
choices.consequence: How hard can it be to find one lost sticky note?

nodes.title: The Backpack of Preparedness
nodes.prose:
You lunge for your backpack — the blue one hanging on the bathroom door — and manage to grab it as the portal sucks you in. You tumble through the swirling purple tunnel with the backpack clutched to your chest.

You land with a THUMP on something crunchy. You look down. You are sitting in a field of enormous glowing mushrooms, each one the size of a garden shed, each glowing a different colour.

CRUNCH! SQUELCH! POP!

You've landed on a medium-sized purple mushroom. It fires you three feet into the air. You land on the grass. "Ow," you say.

"Impressive landing," says a voice. Sitting on the largest blue mushroom is a creature that looks like a cross between a raccoon and a wizard — small, pointy-eared, covered in stripy fur, wearing a hat absolutely covered in badges: "WORLD'S OKAYEST GUIDE" and "I SURVIVED THE CHEESE INCIDENT OF '09."

"Name's Scritchy," says the creature, tipping his hat. "Interdimensional tour guide, occasional potion tester, full-time lover of snacks. You've arrived in the Mushroom Borderlands."

He eyes your backpack approvingly. Inside: one slightly squashed cheese sandwich, a library book two weeks overdue, a torch, some string, and Professor Biscuit's emergency wheel. Scritchy lights up. "The STRING! The cheese sandwich — we'll need it for the Crust Trolls. Right then. Two ways forward."
nodes.imagePrompt: A kid landing on a giant glowing purple mushroom in a magical forest of enormous colourful mushrooms each the size of a shed, a small raccoon-wizard creature with a badge-covered hat sitting nearby, vibrant cartoon illustration style, whimsical children's book art

choices.text: Through the glowing mushroom forest toward the Robot Jungle
choices.consequence: Trees made of robot arms. It's fine. Probably.

choices.text: Down into the Cheese Caverns with the Crust Trolls
choices.consequence: The walls glow yellow. Do NOT lick them.

nodes.title: Parmelius the Aromatic
nodes.prose:
Parmelius the wizard is four thousand and thirty-seven years old. He is very small, very wrinkled, and smells exactly like a cheese shop on a warm Tuesday. His tower is made of crystallised cloud and leaning slightly to the left.

"WHO DARES," thunders Parmelius, opening the door before you even knock, "TO DISTURB MY AFTERNOON CHEESE?"

"Hi," you say. "Your cheese moon is falling on us. Can you stop it?"

A very long pause. Parmelius's extremely impressive eyebrows migrate upward. "The cheese moon? That's still going? I made that in 2024. Cloud years. I thought it had burned up by now."

He strokes his enormously long beard. "I remember the counter-spell. There are two versions. One requires a specific ingredient I happen to have. The other requires the Legendary Fart Crystal."

"What ingredient do you have?" Parmelius holds up a jar. Inside is something yellow and extremely jiggly.

"Belly button fluff," he says, with great academic pride. "Specifically yours. Collected from the prophecy archives. Eleven-year-old belly button fluff is the most magically potent substance in seventeen galaxies. I need you to donate some. Voluntarily. It will tingle."
nodes.imagePrompt: A tiny ancient wizard with enormous eyebrows and an incredibly long beard standing in a leaning crystallised tower, holding up a jar of glowing yellow fluff, looking delighted, a kid standing at the door looking alarmed, vibrant cartoon illustration style

choices.text: Donate your belly button fluff for the greater good (it only tingles a bit)
choices.consequence: For seventeen galaxies. Worth it.

choices.text: Ask about the Legendary Fart Crystal instead — sounds more impressive
choices.consequence: Created by the First Wizard eating an entire mountain of magical beans.

nodes.title: The Robot Jungle of Mechazorbia
nodes.prose:
The robot jungle is INCREDIBLE. Trees made of robot arms wave slowly in the wind, each hand opening and closing. Robot birds with camera eyes tweet in binary (it sounds like a dial-up modem having a lovely time).

"Stay on the path! Don't touch anything that looks at you! And DEFINITELY don't challenge the Chess-Bot to chess," says Scritchy. "It hasn't lost in nine hundred years and it gets weird about it."

You stay on the path. You manage not to touch anything that looks at you. And then you round a corner and there is an enormous golden robot sitting in a clearing, playing chess against itself, muttering.

The robot looks up. Its eyes flash yellow. "HUMAN. Do you play chess?"

"I know the moves," you say carefully. Scritchy is windmilling all four arms frantically behind you.

"If you beat me," says the Chess-Bot, "I will give you safe passage to the Fart Crystal and restore the dimensional balance. If I win... you must become my Chess Coach for one year."

One year. You'd miss loads of school. Honestly that sounds fine. Scritchy is now lying flat on the ground making "please no" gestures.
nodes.imagePrompt: A vast jungle where all trees are made of giant robot arms waving, an enormous golden chess-playing robot sitting in a clearing looking at a kid intensely, a small raccoon-wizard creature lying flat on the ground in despair, vibrant cartoon illustration style

choices.text: Accept the chess challenge — you have a plan
choices.consequence: The plan involves inventing new rules on the spot.

choices.text: Politely decline and sneak around the long way through the jungle
choices.consequence: Sneaking is an underrated heroic skill.

nodes.title: The Cheese Caverns and the Crust Trolls
nodes.prose:
The Cheese Caverns smell like the inside of a crisp packet, but turned up to eleven. The walls glow faintly yellow and orange. The floor is springy. You bounce slightly with every step, which is actually quite fun.

Scritchy unwraps your cheese sandwich as you walk. "For the Crust Trolls," he explains. "They worship bread crusts. It's religious. Don't joke about it."

The Crust Trolls are approximately the height of a wellington boot, rock-grey, with enormous noses and very tiny mouths. Their leader — wearing a crust crown — steps forward. "TOLL! To pass the deep cavern, you pay the GREAT BREAD TOLL."

Scritchy presents the cheese sandwich crusts with enormous solemnity. The Troll King examines them. Sniffs them. His tiny eyes go wide.

"Cheese on the crusts," he breathes. "CHEESE. We have not seen cheese crusts since the Ancient Cheese Times. These are holy."

He looks up. "PROPHET OF CHEESE! You shall pass! But first — we have a QUEST for you!"

The Troll King points down two tunnels. In the left tunnel: a rumbling, distant roar. In the right tunnel: a golden glow and what sounds suspiciously like party music.
nodes.imagePrompt: Glowing yellow and orange underground cheese caverns, springy cheese floor, tiny rock-grey troll creatures with enormous noses and a crust crown on their leader, a kid and a raccoon-wizard creature presenting a cheese sandwich with great ceremony, vibrant cartoon illustration style

choices.text: Take the left tunnel toward the rumbling — sounds like adventure
choices.consequence: That rhythm. That's... snoring.

choices.text: Take the right tunnel toward the golden glow and party music
choices.consequence: They have been partying for two years. Waiting for you.

nodes.title: The Legendary Fart Crystal
nodes.prose:
"Tell me about the Fart Crystal," you say. Parmelius's eyes light up. He has clearly been waiting for someone to ask this for approximately four thousand years.

"The Great Fart Crystal of Destiny," he begins, pulling out a scroll so long it unfurls across the floor, "was created by the First Wizard of this dimension after he consumed an entire mountain of magical beans. The resulting event — which lasted forty-seven minutes and registered on instruments in four galaxies — crystallised into a gem of pure ancient energy."

"When activated by the correct phrase, it can push the cheese moon back?"

"Yes." He hesitates. "The phrase is... somewhat embarrassing."

"Tell me." He whispers it. You blink. You blink again. "I have to say THAT? Out loud? In front of people?"

"The crystal can only be activated by someone willing to completely abandon their dignity in the service of others," says Parmelius gently. "It is, in a sense, the ultimate test of heroism."

You look out the window. The cheese moon is enormous now, filling half the sky, smelling like a warm fondue. You have seventeen galaxies depending on you.
nodes.imagePrompt: A tiny ancient wizard unrolling an enormous scroll covered in mystical diagrams, a glowing green crystal on a pedestal in the background, a kid looking shocked at something being whispered to them, vibrant cartoon illustration style, whimsical children's book art

choices.text: Say the extremely embarrassing phrase with your full chest
choices.consequence: Dignity: sacrificed. Galaxies: saved.

choices.text: Find a DIFFERENT way — maybe physics can solve this instead
choices.consequence: What if you made the OTHER side heavier?

nodes.title: The Unspeakable Wiggle Saves the World
nodes.prose:
"I'll figure it out," you say.

You begin. Step one is a shimmy. Easy. Step two is a clockwise wobble. Getting there. Step three involves your elbows in a way that isn't technically legal in most dimensions. Step seven is just labelled "COMMIT." You commit.

And then: THE UNSPEAKABLE WIGGLE.

Nobody can describe what step nine looks like. Your entire body vibrates at a frequency previously unknown to science. The Cloud King gasps. Flumf actually falls off the cloud. Every bird in Fluffaris takes flight simultaneously.

BOOM. A beam of pure blue light fires from your belly button, hits the Repulsion Beacon on the palace roof, and sends a perfect bolt of energy directly at the Sky Cheese Moon.

The moon shudders. Wobbles. And begins to slowly drift back into space. The crowd goes absolutely berserk. The Cloud King cries. Flumf hugs you so hard your bones creak.

You are awarded the Medal of the Magnificent Belly Button. It is made of cloud gold. It is the size of a bin lid. You can never wear it to school because nobody would believe you, and that is somehow the funniest thing of all.

Zorbax the toilet sends a dimensional postcard. It says: "Told you so." You pin it to your wall.
nodes.imagePrompt: A kid doing an incredible dance move with a beam of blue light shooting from their belly button toward a giant cheese moon in the sky, a crowd of round cloud creatures cheering wildly, vibrant cartoon illustration style, epic and triumphant

nodes.title: The Legendary Burp Duke Lives Again
nodes.prose:
"Is there ANY other way?" you ask. Flumf scratches his head with all four arms.

"Well... there IS the old emergency activation. But nobody's used it in eight hundred years."

"What is it?"

"A burp," says Flumf. "Specifically, a burp in the key of G flat, sustained for at least four seconds, aimed directly at the beacon crystal. But the last person who could do it was the Legendary Burp Duke of Old Fluffaris, and he retired to a quiet cloud in the countryside."

You put your hand up slowly. "I can do that."

Silence.

"You can burp in G flat?"

"I once burped the entire first verse of a birthday song. My dad was very proud. My mum was not."

They stare at you. You drink the largest glass of fizzy cloud juice Flumf can find. You aim yourself at the beacon. You focus. You dig deep. You find the G flat.

BWUUUUUUUUURRRRRRRRP!!!!!

It shakes the palace. It shakes three neighbouring clouds. The beacon activates. The cheese moon retreats. They build a statue of you. It depicts you mid-burp. Your expression is one of profound concentration and mild embarrassment. You are extremely proud.
nodes.imagePrompt: A kid mid-enormous-burp with sound waves visible radiating outward, hitting a glowing beacon crystal, cloud creatures covering their ears but cheering, vibrant cartoon illustration style, gross and glorious

nodes.title: The Mighty Slug Gerald Saves the Day
nodes.prose:
"Let's find that password," you say.

You and Flumf search the Cloud Palace. You find 47 cloud biscuits (eaten). You find a trumpet shaped like a fish. You find a painting of the Cloud King that appears to wink at you. You find a storage room full of catapults labelled "DO NOT USE NEAR CHEESE MOON" — someone has clearly already used them near the cheese moon.

You find a note on the Cloud King's desk: "Password hint: it is the thing I love most, but written backwards."

"What does the Cloud King love most?" you ask. Flumf thinks. "He loves three things equally: thunder, biscuits, and his pet cloud-slug named Gerald."

You try REDNUHT. Nothing. You try STIUCSIB. Nothing. You try DLAREEG.

DING! BEEP-BOOP! WHIRRRR!

The Repulsion Beacon makes a sound like a happy kettle and a green light blinks on.

"Gerald," says Flumf softly. "It was always Gerald."

The beacon fires. The cheese moon wobbles and retreats into orbit. The Cloud King promotes Gerald to Royal Cloud Slug and First Minister of Passwords. Gerald celebrates by doing what slugs do, which is very slowly going somewhere. You get home by tea time.
nodes.imagePrompt: A kid triumphantly typing a password into a glowing control panel, a chubby cloud slug wearing a tiny crown nearby, a four-armed alien creature with tears of joy, vibrant cartoon illustration style, silly and triumphant

nodes.title: The Most Powerful Substance in 17 Galaxies
nodes.prose:
"Fine," you say. "For seventeen galaxies. Take the fluff."

Parmelius produces a tiny golden spoon and a velvet-lined box. He approaches your belly button with the gravity of a surgeon and the excitement of someone about to unwrap a Christmas present. It does tingle. A lot. But the fluff he extracts glows like a tiny star in the box.

"MAGNIFICENT," breathes Parmelius. "This is the most potent belly button fluff I have seen in four thousand years. The colour! The texture! The mild cheesy aroma!"

"Please never describe it again," you say.

He drops the fluff into a bubbling cauldron along with things you choose not to examine. The cauldron roars. A beam of emerald light fires upward through the tower roof and hits the cheese moon.

KAZOOOOM! PLINK! SHWABBADABBA!

The cheese moon seals itself back into a stable orbit.

Parmelius offers to write up the research. You make him promise to call it something other than "Thunderbottom's Remarkable Fluff." He promises. The paper is published as "{PLAYER_NAME}'s Remarkable Fluff." You are both embarrassed and quietly delighted.

Your belly button is fine. It just glows faintly on Tuesdays now. Nobody has noticed yet.
nodes.imagePrompt: A tiny ancient wizard extracting glowing belly button fluff with a golden spoon, dropping it into a bubbling magical cauldron that fires an emerald beam through the roof, a kid watching with resigned dignity, vibrant cartoon illustration style

nodes.title: Chaos Chess Conquers the Undefeated
nodes.prose:
You sit down across from the Chess-Bot. Scritchy has apparently fainted somewhere behind you.

"I accept your challenge," you say. "But I have one condition. We play my rules. Every third move, instead of moving a chess piece, you answer a silly question. Get it wrong and you lose a piece."

"I have never played this variant," says the Chess-Bot slowly.

"It's called Chaos Chess. It's very popular on Earth." (It is not. You made it up right now.)

The Chess-Bot agrees, which proves that even nine-hundred-year-old undefeated robot geniuses can be outsmarted by someone willing to invent a rule on the spot.

Question one: "What is the funniest number?" The Chess-Bot calculates for eleven minutes. "...Seven?" You say no. It is clearly eight. The robot loses a bishop.

Question two: "What does a cloud biscuit taste like?" The Chess-Bot has never tasted anything. It loses its queen.

You win in forty-three moves. The Chess-Bot gives you safe passage and also asks to learn more games. You teach it Snap. It beats you at Snap immediately. Some things cannot be stopped. The dimensional balance is restored.
nodes.imagePrompt: A kid playing chess against a huge golden robot, the robot looking confused by a silly question being asked, a small raccoon-wizard creature watching from behind a tree in awe, vibrant cartoon illustration style, clever and triumphant

nodes.title: The Sneak That Saved Everything
nodes.prose:
"No chess," you whisper to Scritchy. "We go around."

Scritchy looks like he might cry with relief. "I have never been more grateful to anyone in my life."

You sneak left through a grove of robot arm trees. The trees wave at you. You wave back because it seems rude not to. You crawl under a laser-wire fence. You jump over a pit of mechanical butterflies (they're lovely, actually, but you don't have time).

And then you find it: a clearing with a plinth, and on the plinth — glowing faintly green, approximately the size of a large potato — the Fart Crystal.

"We just... take it?" you whisper.

"I think so?" says Scritchy.

You pick it up. Nothing explodes. This is a good sign. The crystal hums warmly in your hands and then begins to glow brighter, and brighter, and —

PAAAARP! (A very dignified one, all things considered.)

A beam of green light fires straight up into the sky. Miles away, the cheese moon groans and shifts into safe orbit.

You did it. No chess. No embarrassing phrases. No belly button involvement of any kind. Just good old-fashioned sneaking.

Scritchy gives you his favourite badge: "ACTUALLY PRETTY DECENT." You treasure it forever.
nodes.imagePrompt: A kid sneaking through a forest of robot arm trees, tiptoeing past a giant golden chess robot who isn't looking, a raccoon-wizard creature tiptoeing behind them, vibrant cartoon illustration style, stealthy and triumphant

nodes.title: The Cheese Wyrm's Cheesy Dream
nodes.prose:
The rumbling gets louder as you go deeper. It shakes the cheese walls in a rhythm. Scritchy holds his hat on.

"That rhythm," he says slowly. "That's... snoring."

You round a corner. In a cavern so large it has its own weather, curled around the Fart Crystal like a dog around a favourite toy, is the GREAT CHEESE WYRM. It is roughly the size of four buses, made entirely of living animated cheese, and it is fast asleep, snoring at approximately the volume of a freight train.

The Fart Crystal glows beneath one of its enormous cheesy claws.

You have one of the Troll King's holy bread crusts left in your pocket. You kept one. Just in case.

You place the crust gently under the Wyrm's nose. Its enormous nostrils twitch. Its eyes flutter. And with a sound like a very large fridge falling over, it rolls sideways in its sleep, smiling. The Crystal rolls free.

SNOOOORT — THWUMMMMP!

You grab the Crystal, which activates immediately. The dimensional beam fires. The cosmic cheese is redirected. Everyone is saved. The Cheese Wyrm sleeps on, smiling, dreaming of bread.

Scritchy's badge collection gains one new entry: "CHEESE WYRM WHISPERER."
nodes.imagePrompt: A massive creature made of living cheese curled asleep around a glowing crystal in a huge underground cavern, a kid gently placing a bread crust under its nose, a raccoon-wizard watching with wide eyes, vibrant cartoon illustration style

nodes.title: Dancing Saved Seventeen Galaxies
nodes.prose:
The party music gets louder and the golden glow gets brighter and you push open a door made of crystallised cheddar and find yourself in the most incredible underground party you have ever seen.

There are Crust Trolls everywhere, dancing wildly to music played by a band of robot slug-creatures. Tables covered in every kind of cheese you have ever imagined. Decorations made of bioluminescent moss.

At the centre of the room, spinning slowly on a plinth like a disco ball, is the Fart Crystal. It appears to be powering the whole party.

The Troll King is standing on a table. "THE CHEESE PROPHET ARRIVES! THE PARTY HAS WAITED FOR YOU!"

"The party... was waiting for me?"

"The Crystal sensed your coming. It activated the celebration protocols. We have been partying for two years." He looks slightly tired but happy. "We have so much cheese."

You dance. You eat incredible cheese. Scritchy eats more cheese than should be physically possible for a creature of his size. And at exactly the right moment — just when you're mid-dance-move — the Crystal pulses gold and fires a beam straight through the cave ceiling into space, nudging the cheese catastrophe back into orbit.

This is the best way to save the world. You're almost certain of it.
nodes.imagePrompt: An incredible underground party with tiny rock-grey troll creatures dancing wildly, a glowing crystal spinning like a disco ball on a plinth, tables covered in exotic cheeses, a kid mid-dance-move in the centre, vibrant cartoon illustration style, joyful and chaotic

nodes.title: Dignity: Sacrificed. World: Saved.
nodes.prose:
You take a deep breath. You look at the Crystal. You look at the sky full of incoming cheese. You think about seventeen galaxies.

You say the phrase.

We cannot print the phrase here. This is a story for eight-year-olds and the phrase made Parmelius — four thousand years old and veteran of countless dimensional disasters — cover his face with his hat.

What we CAN tell you is that it rhymes with something hilarious, involves a very specific description of a bottom-related event, and includes the words "magnificently" and "Tuesday."

...

KABOOOOM! (The good kind.)

The Crystal activates. The cheese moon is repelled so hard it bounces three extra dimensions away and parks itself near a completely different galaxy who will have to deal with it now. Good luck to them.

Parmelius publishes your phrase in "The Great Texts of Dimensional Magic." It is in the index under "methods not recommended for polite company."

You are both legendary and slightly embarrassed. This is, you decide, the perfect combination.

Your mum never finds out what you said. Probably.
nodes.imagePrompt: A kid shouting a phrase with full commitment at a glowing crystal, an ancient wizard hiding his face under his hat in shock, a massive beam of energy firing into the sky, vibrant cartoon illustration style, gross and gloriously triumphant

nodes.title: Reverse Cheese Physics Saves the Day
nodes.prose:
"I have a different idea," you say. Parmelius raises his enormous eyebrows.

"The cheese moon is coming down, right? So the problem is gravity. What if we don't push it UP — what if we made it HEAVIER on the other side, so it spins away from us under its own weight?"

Parmelius stares at you. "That is," he says slowly, "either completely wrong or genuinely brilliant. I can't tell which."

"We use the Crystal to fire a gravity pulse from the FAR side of the moon," you continue, warming up. "Pulling that side down, which tilts the moon, which changes its trajectory—"

Parmelius has already started calculating. His quill moves so fast it smokes. "...The angular momentum would... yes... if we account for the cheese density being greater on the brie side... YOU have just invented Reverse Cheese Physics."

He fires the Crystal. The pulse hits the far side of the moon. The moon tilts forty-three degrees. And, very slowly at first and then quite quickly, it spins away into safe orbit.

Parmelius insists you co-author the paper. It wins the Dimensional Science Prize. You use the prize money (17 cloud biscuits and a voucher for thunder) to buy Professor Biscuit a new wheel.

You are eleven years old and you have just invented a new branch of physics. Tomorrow is Tuesday and you have double maths. Life, as always, is wonderfully ridiculous.
